# MARS known-answer vectors, generated by an independent implementation.
#
# Why this file exists: the AES submission published vectors for 128, 192 and
# 256-bit MARS keys only. The v9 paranoia cascade uses 448-bit keys, so nothing
# authoritative covered the key length that actually matters here.
#
# Oracle: Botan 1.10.17, src/block/mars/mars.cpp, (C) 1999-2009 Jack Lloyd,
# Simplified BSD. Archive Botan-1.10.17.tgz from
# https://botan.randombit.net/releases/old/, SHA-256
# 6847ffb64b8d2f939dccfecc17bd2c80385d08f7621e2c56d3a335118e823613.
#
# That oracle is an independent implementation line from Crypto++, and it was
# checked against the published 128-bit vector before being trusted:
# key 80000...0, plaintext 0, ciphertext B3E2AD5608AC1B6733A7CB4FDF8F9952.
# That check matters because Brian Gladman's widely mirrored mars.c predates
# the 22 September 1999 MARS revision and implements the older key schedule; it
# disagrees with both Crypto++ and the published vectors, and would have looked
# like a fault in this repository rather than in the oracle.
#
# Botan is NOT vendored. Only these answers are, so the evidence stays
# reproducible without adding a second cryptography library to the build.
#
# Format: <key hex> <plaintext hex> <ciphertext hex>
